pack.name: AI Governance / Responsible AI
pack.description: Starter baseline for AI/ML asset governance — model inventory, data handling, human oversight, and risk classification. Maps to NIST AI RMF v1.0 themes and EU AI Act high-risk categories. Not a compliance certification.

rules.title: AI model registry documented
rules.description: The architecture manifest should identify AI/ML assets (models, endpoints, or inference services) with enough specificity that operators can maintain an inventory; anonymized placeholders are insufficient when production reliance is claimed.
rules.remediationGuidance: Enumerate inference/training surfaces under services[] (ServiceName, Purpose, Tags) and tie each to an owning team in governance.RequiredControls or governance.PolicyConstraints.

frameworkMappings.category: Annex III — AI systems intended for critical infrastructure / safety-related contexts (thematic mapping)

rules.title: Model ownership assigned
rules.description: Each material AI component should have accountable ownership reflected in governance metadata so escalation and change control have a named lever.
rules.remediationGuidance: Add ownership statements to governance.PolicyConstraints or governance.RequiredControls (e.g., owner:RACI) and reference the same language in metadata.ChangeDescription for the snapshot.

frameworkMappings.category: Annex III — High-risk administrative / operational reliance (thematic mapping)

rules.title: Model versioning tracked
rules.description: Model lifecycle posture should capture version or promotion lineage so reviewers can distinguish experiments from approved production configurations.
rules.remediationGuidance: Record promotion lineage using metadata.ManifestVersion, metadata.ParentManifestVersion, and explicit notes in metadata.ChangeDescription linking services to approved versions.

rules.title: Deployment environments documented
rules.description: Inference and training boundaries across environments (dev/test/stage/prod) must be understandable from the manifest to avoid shadow production AI paths.
rules.remediationGuidance: Describe environment separation in governance.PolicyConstraints and align services[].RuntimePlatform / Purpose with environment labels in Tags.

rules.title: Sensitive training data justified when present
rules.description: When training or fine-tuning touches personally identifiable or protected health information, the manifest should document proportionality and routing—not silent inclusion.
rules.remediationGuidance: Capture minimization rationale in governance.PolicyConstraints; tag affected datastores and flows in relationships with governance.ComplianceTags citing handling constraints.

frameworkMappings.category: Data governance & fundamental rights themes (thematic mapping)

rules.title: Data classification prior to inference
rules.description: Flows into inference should reflect classification posture so reviewers can see whether sensitive categories are routed through controlled interfaces.
rules.remediationGuidance: Use governance.ComplianceTags for classification tiers and reinforce per-service controls via services[].RequiredControls for inference APIs.

rules.title: Sensitive data routing documented
rules.description: Architecture graphs should expose routing decisions for regulated payloads (PHI/PII/financial identifiers) touching AI surfaces.
rules.remediationGuidance: Document routing and segmentation expectations in governance.PolicyConstraints and bind them to concrete edges in relationships plus datastore roles.

rules.title: Human sign-off before production promotion
rules.description: Production promotion of high-impact models should show human governance signals in manifest provenance—not only automated pipeline success.
rules.remediationGuidance: Reference approver lineage through metadata.DecisionTraceIds and narrate promotion decisions in metadata.ChangeDescription; elevate governance.RiskClassification when impact increases.

rules.title: High-risk automated decisions reviewed by humans
rules.description: When services encode consequential scoring or triage, the manifest should indicate human review gates appropriate to potential harm.
rules.remediationGuidance: Encode review expectations in governance.RequiredControls and mirror with service-level Tags describing HITL checkpoints on affected services[].

frameworkMappings.category: Annex III — Access to essential services / automated decision themes (thematic mapping)

rules.title: Override and escalation path documented
rules.description: Operators need a documented path to challenge, override, or escalate unsafe model behavior without bypassing auditability.
rules.remediationGuidance: Describe override workflow in governance.PolicyConstraints; link accountable parties using governance.RequiredControls with clear verbs (escalate, freeze, rollback).

rules.title: Review cadence defined
rules.description: Model governance should state how often stakeholders re-validate suitability, drift tolerances, and data policy alignment.
rules.remediationGuidance: Add cadence statements to governance.PolicyConstraints and optionally surface schedule hints in advisoryDefaults-compatible metadata via pack publish (operational checklist).

rules.title: Model evaluation cadence defined
rules.description: Evaluation discipline (offline/online metrics) should be visible to reviewers even when metrics live outside the manifest literal.
rules.remediationGuidance: Capture evaluation commitments in governance.RequiredControls and cross-reference owning services with services[].Tags (eval:*).

rules.title: Drift monitoring described
rules.description: Production AI services should declare how drift is observed and tied back to governance triggers.
rules.remediationGuidance: Add drift monitoring obligations to governance.RequiredControls and mention telemetry surfaces in services[].RequiredControls.

rules.title: Retraining triggers documented
rules.description: When models retrain automatically or on schedule, reviewers need explicit thresholds or events justifying refreshes.
rules.remediationGuidance: Encode retrain triggers in governance.PolicyConstraints and align with metadata.ChangeDescription when manifest updates follow retrain events.

rules.title: LLM interactions logged
rules.description: Generative flows should point to logging and traceability mechanisms so prompts, outputs, and session context can be audited where policy requires.
rules.remediationGuidance: Tag LLM gateways with logging expectations in services[].Tags and governance.RequiredControls; reference decision tracing with metadata.DecisionTraceIds.

rules.title: Retention policy for AI logs defined
rules.description: Retention for model and prompt telemetry should be stated to avoid indefinite storage of sensitive transcripts.
rules.remediationGuidance: State retention bounds in governance.PolicyConstraints; tag storage services in services[].Tags (retention:*).

rules.title: Tool invocation audit trail
rules.description: Agentic tool calls (search, APIs, runners) should be traceable with the same stewardship as raw inference when used in regulated workflows.
rules.remediationGuidance: Document tool-call trace requirements in governance.RequiredControls; link orchestration services with services[].Purpose and services[].Tags including tool-chain identifiers.

rules.title: Third-party model risk assessed
rules.description: External models or APIs should carry documented risk posture and dependency depth visible in governance metadata.
rules.remediationGuidance: Capture vendor/model risk statements in governance.ComplianceTags and governance.PolicyConstraints; flag third-party services via services[].Tags (vendor:*).

rules.title: Vendor dependency and fallback strategy
rules.description: Single-vendor AI lock-in without fallback violates resilient enterprise practice; manifests should show mitigations.
rules.remediationGuidance: Describe fallback or degraded modes in governance.PolicyConstraints; map alternate routes in relationships and annotate services[].RequiredControls.

rules.title: SLA and availability expectations documented
rules.description: Business-critical AI endpoints should tie to availability expectations understandable from architecture metadata.
rules.remediationGuidance: Record SLA themes in governance.PolicyConstraints and cost/operational posture using governance.CostClassification plus services[].Tags for tiering.

frameworkMappings.category: High reliability / critical service themes (thematic mapping)
